reasoning: The candidate overreads “independently” as unconditional payout availability for every recipient accepted at creation. The controlling context says both “Sponsor and treasury can claim independently after settlement” and, immediately afterward, “Never move assets between raffle clones” (target/DESIGN.md:L2, sentences 14–15). Read together, independence concerns claim ordering and separate entitlements; it does not authorize payment to an address that has since become another raffle clone. The implementation allocates separate balances (target/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:L551-L555), and each release reads and clears only its own balance (L375-L391). In the proposed future-clone scenario, sponsor release is rejected solely by the destination classifier (L564-L566, L593-L604), regardless of whether treasury has claimed; the treasury claim neither consumes nor blocks the sponsor entitlement. That scenario enforces the adjacent inter-clone-transfer prohibition rather than demonstrating dependence between the two claims, so the REQ-46 divergence should be dropped.
